IB Economics SL
Australia’s 2024-25 Federal Budget

The Australian government is proposing a deficit budget. Is expansionary fiscal policy the appropriate choice for Australia?

How do I use this resource?

Guiding Question

Discuss the impact of expansionary fiscal policy on housing prices in Australia.

a

easy

Define the term budget deficit. [2]

Answer


Show / Hide Mark Scheme

Mark Scheme

Sample answer‾\underline{\textrm{Sample answer}}Sample answer​:

The AU$\text{\textdollar}$1.9 billion spent in the Commonwealth Rent Assistance program aims at providing support for renters, covering part of their rent. As this form of transfer payment goes directly to renters, it would increase the demand for housing. The consequent rightward shift of the demand curve would result in higher prices of housing, further reducing their affordability in the country.


Explanation‾\underline{\textrm{Explanation}}Explanation​:

For drawing a fully labelled D/S diagram showing

  • a rightward shift of the demand curve (✓\checkmark✓)
  • a higher price and quantity of houses (✓\checkmark✓)

For explaining that, by providing AU$\text{\textdollar}$1.9 billion in rent assistance, there will likely be an increase in the demand for housing (rightward shift) (✓\checkmark✓)

For explaining that this will cause an increase in the price of housing, which will likely worsen housing affordability in Australia (✓\checkmark✓)

Mark Scheme

Sample answer‾\underline{\textrm{Sample answer}}Sample answer​:

Budget deficit refers to a situation in which a government’s expenditures exceed its revenues, requiring the government to borrow money to cover the difference.


Explanation‾\underline{\textrm{Explanation}}Explanation​:

For defining a budget deficit as

  • greater government spending than government revenues (✓\checkmark✓)
  • necessitating government borrowing to cover the difference (✓\checkmark✓)

b

easy

Explain why a budget deficit can be considered an expansionary fiscal policy. [3]

Answer


Show / Hide Mark Scheme

Mark Scheme

Sample answer‾\underline{\textrm{Sample answer}}Sample answer​:

Two stakeholders that are negatively affected are firms having late employees due to the longer commuting time and children whose education is affected.

The Australian government plans on addressing this problem by training more construction workers and providing more housing-enabling infrastructures, which will promote the construction of new housing. This will encourage labour force participation in the economy and reduce travel time, which will likely result in increased productivity in the economy. As it will cause a rightward shift of the AS curve, it can be regarded as a supply-side policy.


Explanation‾\underline{\textrm{Explanation}}Explanation​:

For stating two stakeholders who are negatively affected by the lack of affordable housing (✓\checkmark✓ ✓\checkmark✓)

Possible answers include:

  • Firms facing reduced productivity
  • Firms having late employees
  • Local communities damaged by more traffic
  • Increased public spending in healthcare
  • Lower tax revenues due to lower labour force participation
  • Disruptions in children’s education

For explaining that government policies to address the housing shortage comprise training more construction workers and providing more housing-enabling infrastructures (✓\checkmark✓)

or

For explaining that more affordable housing will boost labour force participation in the economy, reduce travel time and increase social mobility (✓\checkmark✓)

For explaining that these factors can be considered part of a supply-side policy since they allow workers to be more productive and increase the economy’s productive capacity (✓\checkmark✓)

Mark Scheme

Sample answer‾\underline{\textrm{Sample answer}}Sample answer​:

A budget deficit can occur as a result of an increase in government spending or a decrease in government revenues due to lower taxation. These can be regarded as expansionary policy measures as they would cause the aggregate demand (AD) curve to shift rightward, boosting the country’s real GDP.


Explanation‾\underline{\textrm{Explanation}}Explanation​:

For explaining that a budget deficit would arise from greater government spending or lower tax levels (✓\checkmark✓)

For explaining that policies changing the levels of government spending or taxation are examples of fiscal policy (✓\checkmark✓)

For explaining these changes would cause a rightward shift of the AD curve, increasing the country’s real GDP and causing economic growth, which explains why this is an example of an expansionary fiscal policy (✓\checkmark✓)

Calculate the average income tax rate for someone earning AU$\text{\textdollar}$40 000 in 2025. [4]

Answer


Show / Hide Mark Scheme

Mark Scheme

Sample answer‾\underline{\textrm{Sample answer}}Sample answer​:

Basic foods such as rice, wheat or potatoes are typically consumed more by low-income households. This means that a 10% GST on basic food would greatly affect poorer families, with the tax taking up a larger proportion of their income compared to richer families. This makes the GST a regressive tax, further increasing wealth inequality in the country.


Explanation‾\underline{\textrm{Explanation}}Explanation​:

For explaining that low-income households tend to spend a greater proportion of their income on basic foods (✓\checkmark✓)

For explaining that a 10% GST on basic foods would take up a greater proportion of the income for poorer families, making it a regressive tax (✓\checkmark✓)

For explaining that the regressive nature of the tax would increase wealth inequality in the country (✓\checkmark✓)

Mark Scheme

Sample answer‾\underline{\textrm{Sample answer}}Sample answer​:

Someone earning AU$\text{\textdollar}$40 000 in 2025 would have AU$\text{\textdollar}$18 200 falling in first income bracket, paying AU$18 200 ×\text{\textdollar}18\ 200 \ \times$18 200 × 0% = AU$\text{\textdollar}$0.

The remaining of AU$\text{\textdollar}$21 800 falls entirely into the second income bracket, paying AU$21800 ×\text{\textdollar}21 800 \ \times$21800 × 16% = AU$\text{\textdollar}$3 488.

The average tax is AU$0+AU$3 488AU$40 000\dfrac{\ce{AU\text{\textdollar}0 + AU\text{\textdollar}3 488}}{\ce{AU\text{\textdollar}40 000}}AU$40 000AU$0+AU$3 488​ = 0.0872 = 8.72%.


Explanation‾\underline{\textrm{Explanation}}Explanation​:

The total tax comes from the tax paid for each income bracket as

AU$18 200 ×\text{\textdollar}18\ 200\ \times$18 200 × 0% +(AU$\text{\textdollar}$40 000 - AU$18 200) ×\text{\textdollar}18\ 200)\ \times$18 200) × 16% = AU$3 488

For applying the correct formula (✓\checkmark✓)
For calculating the correct result (✓\checkmark✓)

The average tax rate for an income of AU$\text{\textdollar}$40 000 is

AU$0+AU$3 488AU$40 000\dfrac{\ce{AU\text{\textdollar}0 + AU\text{\textdollar}3 488}}{\ce{AU\text{\textdollar}40 000}}AU$40 000AU$0+AU$3 488​ = 0.0872 = = 8.72%

For applying the correct formula (✓\checkmark✓)
For calculating the correct result (✓\checkmark✓)

d

medium

Explain why the income tax rates in 2025 would likely promote equity but not equality in Australia. [4]

Answer


Show / Hide Mark Scheme

Mark Scheme

Sample answer‾\underline{\textrm{Sample answer}}Sample answer​:

Equality means that everyone is treated in the same way, which does not occur for the income tax rates in 2025 as high-income people contribute a significantly larger proportion of their income compared to low-income ones.

Equity focuses on addressing individual needs and differences to achieve fairness, even if it may involve unequal treatment. The 2025 income tax system imposes higher rates on higher earners, reflecting their greater ability to contribute compared to those with lower incomes.


Explanation‾\underline{\textrm{Explanation}}Explanation​:

For explaining that equality means that everyone is treated in the same way (✓\checkmark✓)

For explaining that the income tax rates for 2025 would not promote equality since high-income individuals pay a higher percentage compared to low-income individuals (✓\checkmark✓)

For explaining that equity acknowledges differences and eliminates disparities to reach fairness (✓\checkmark✓)

For explaining that the income tax system for 2025 would promote equity as tax rates increase with the income as richer people have a greater ability to pay compared to poorer ones (✓\checkmark✓)

Text
​

Australia’s 2024-25 Federal Budget

In May 2024, the Australian government presented its 2024-25 federal budget proposal, predicting a deficit of AU$\text{\textdollar}$28.3 billion. The proposal highlighted current challenges such as global tensions and supply chain disruptions, which have adversely affected the economy in 2024. Despite these hurdles, the government forecasted modest economic growth of slightly above 2% for 2025. While inflation eased in 2024, energy bills and housing costs have remained high, contributing to the cost-of-living crisis many Australians are still facing today.

  1. Define the term budget deficit. [2]

  2. Explain why a budget deficit can be considered an expansionary fiscal policy. [3]


One of the policies in the 2024-25 budget is a reduction in the rate of income tax for low earners. The tables show the marginal income tax rates for Australia in 2024 and 2025.

Income (AU$)Marginal tax rates for 2024
0 - 18 2000%
18 201 - 45 00019%
45 001 - 120 00032.5%
120 001 - 180 00037%
180 000 +45%


Income (AU$)Marginal tax rates for 2025
0 - 18 2000%
18 201 - 45 00016%
45 001 - 120 00030%
120 001 - 180 00037%
180 000 +45%

  1. Calculate the average income tax rate for someone earning AU$\text{\textdollar}$40 000 in 2025. [3]

  2. Explain why the income tax rates in 2025 would likely promote equity but not equality in Australia. [4]


The Goods and Services Tax (GST) is Australia's equivalent of the British Value-Added Tax (VAT). It applies at a standard rate of 10% to most goods and services sold or consumed in Australia. However, certain items, including basic food and specific medicines, are exempt from this tax.

  1. Explain why expanding the GST to include basic foods would increase wealth inequality in Australia. [3]


The 2024-25 budget allocated considerable financial resources to address Australia’s housing crisis, which has been exacerbated by a persistent shortage of homes, driving up costs for renters and first-time buyers. This issue has broader productivity, health, and social implications, as the increased commute time and travel costs discourage labour force participation and weaken social mobility. By prioritising stable and affordable housing, the government aims to support workers in securing meaningful employment and minimise disruptions to children's education, fostering long-term societal and economic benefits.

Figure 1 summarises three policy measures meant to address the housing shortage and consequential affordability crisis in Australia.

Policy measureIntended consequenceEstimated cost
Training more construction workersIncreased funding to offer more training incentivesAU$\text{\textdollar}$88.8 million
Housing Support ProgramAdditional funding for states and territories to deliver more housing-enabling infrastructure such as roads, sewers, energy, water, and community infrastructures.AU$\text{\textdollar}$1 billion
10% increase in the Commonwealth Rent Assistance programAdditional financial support for renters to cover part of their rent.AU$\text{\textdollar}$1.9 billion

  1. List two stakeholders who are negatively impacted by the lack of affordable housing, and explain why government policies aimed at solving this problem can be regarded as a supply-side policy. [4]

  2. Using a D/S diagram, explain why the proposed policy measures may fail in reducing the cost of housing in Australia. [4]

Basic foods such as rice, wheat or potatoes are typically consumed more by low-income households. This means that a 10% GST on basic food would greatly affect poorer families, with the tax taking up a larger proportion of their income compared to richer families. This makes the GST a regressive tax, further increasing wealth inequality in the country.

List two stakeholders who are negatively impacted by the lack of affordable housing, and explain why government policies aimed at solving this problem can be regarded as a supply-side policy. [4]

Answer


Show / Hide Mark Scheme

Mark Scheme

Sample answer‾\underline{\textrm{Sample answer}}Sample answer​:

A budget deficit can occur as a result of an increase in government spending or a decrease in government revenues due to lower taxation. These can be regarded as expansionary policy measures as they would cause the aggregate demand (AD) curve to shift rightward, boosting the country’s real GDP.


Explanation‾\underline{\textrm{Explanation}}Explanation​:

For explaining that a budget deficit would arise from greater government spending or lower tax levels (✓\checkmark✓)

For explaining that policies changing the levels of government spending or taxation are examples of fiscal policy (✓\checkmark✓)

For explaining these changes would cause a rightward shift of the AD curve, increasing the country’s real GDP and causing economic growth, which explains why this is an example of an expansionary fiscal policy (✓\checkmark✓)

Mark Scheme

Sample answer‾\underline{\textrm{Sample answer}}Sample answer​:

Two stakeholders that are negatively affected are firms having late employees due to the longer commuting time and children whose education is affected.

The Australian government plans on addressing this problem by training more construction workers and providing more housing-enabling infrastructures, which will promote the construction of new housing. This will encourage labour force participation in the economy and reduce travel time, which will likely result in increased productivity in the economy. As it will cause a rightward shift of the AS curve, it can be regarded as a supply-side policy.


Explanation‾\underline{\textrm{Explanation}}Explanation​:

For stating two stakeholders who are negatively affected by the lack of affordable housing (✓\checkmark✓ ✓\checkmark✓)

Possible answers include:

  • Firms facing reduced productivity
  • Firms having late employees
  • Local communities damaged by more traffic
  • Increased public spending in healthcare
  • Lower tax revenues due to lower labour force participation
  • Disruptions in children’s education

For explaining that government policies to address the housing shortage comprise training more construction workers and providing more housing-enabling infrastructures (✓\checkmark✓)

or

For explaining that more affordable housing will boost labour force participation in the economy, reduce travel time and increase social mobility (✓\checkmark✓)

For explaining that these factors can be considered part of a supply-side policy since they allow workers to be more productive and increase the economy’s productive capacity (✓\checkmark✓)

Sample answer‾\underline{\textrm{Sample answer}}Sample answer​:

The AU$\text{\textdollar}$1.9 billion spent in the Commonwealth Rent Assistance program aims at providing support for renters, covering part of their rent. As this form of transfer payment goes directly to renters, it would increase the demand for housing. The consequent rightward shift of the demand curve would result in higher prices of housing, further reducing their affordability in the country.


Explanation‾\underline{\textrm{Explanation}}Explanation​:

For drawing a fully labelled D/S diagram showing

  • a rightward shift of the demand curve (✓\checkmark✓)
  • a higher price and quantity of houses (✓\checkmark✓)

For explaining that, by providing AU$\text{\textdollar}$1.9 billion in rent assistance, there will likely be an increase in the demand for housing (rightward shift) (✓\checkmark✓)

For explaining that this will cause an increase in the price of housing, which will likely worsen housing affordability in Australia (✓\checkmark✓)
